passages.heard: Napoleon sits down to play chess against a machine.  Legend says he cheats, on purpose, and the machine sweeps every piece right off the board!
This is the Turk, a mechanical man in a turban,  sitting on a big wooden cabinet full of gears.  Built in 1770, it amazed people across Europe and America  for over 80 years.
People said it had to be a trick.  So the showman opened every door  and shone a candle right through.  Nothing in there but gears.  Then he'd wind it up and it would play.  And it usually won.

You see, it was like a magic box with a false bottom.  Hidden inside was a real chess master on a sliding seat.  As each door opened, he slid out of sight.  Magnets under the board showed him every move  and levers worked the arm.
In 1854, the Turk burned in a museum fire.  Later, the secret came out,  and today, Amazon runs a service  where hidden humans do the work computers can't.  Its name?  Mechanical Turk.
